meta.title: Lancashire local government reorganisation: unitary models
meta.summary: On 16 July 2026 the government announced its decision to replace Lancashire's two-tier structure (Lancashire County Council + 12 districts) plus the two existing unitaries (Blackburn with Darwen, Blackpool) with four new unitary councils. This file holds the geography of that decided model and the competing 3- and 5-unitary options submitted during the process, for predictive comparison.

process_timeline.decision_status: Subject to Parliamentary approval; legally confirmed only once a Structural Change Order is made.

meta.name_caveat: None of the unitary names below are statutory. The six sponsoring councils' business case used North Lancashire / Fylde Coast / South Lancashire / East Lancashire; the county council's post-decision press release used North / West / East / South Lancashire, which confusingly reuses 'West Lancashire' for both a new unitary and a folded-in district. ('Pennine Lancashire' is the name of the rejected 3-unitary model's eastern unit, not a 4-unitary unit.) Preston's leader has said publicly it is 'too early to even know what our new unitary authority's name will be'. Treat all labels as working geographic shorthand only.

sources.label: Lancaster City Council LGR committee report, 26 Nov 2025
Lancashire County Council news release, 16 July 2026
MHCLG consultation portal: Lancashire, Blackburn with Darwen, Blackpool
English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (legislation.gov.uk): reforms mayoral/PCC voting to the supplementary vote, leaves principal-council elections on first-past-the-post

four-unitary.label: Four-unitary model
four-unitary.status_note: Selected by the government on 16 July 2026, subject to a Structural Change Order. This is the model that will hold shadow-authority elections in May 2027.
four-unitary.proposer: Chorley, Lancaster, Preston, Ribble Valley, South Ribble and West Lancashire councils ('Four Lancashire for the Future')

three-unitary.label: Three-unitary model
three-unitary.status_note: A competing submission; not selected by the government. Groupings from the Lancaster City Council LGR report, 26 Nov 2025 (para 15b); unit names corroborated via contemporaneous coverage.
three-unitary.proposer: Wyre, Blackburn with Darwen, Hyndburn, Fylde and Rossendale councils

five-unitary.label: Five-unitary model
five-unitary.status_note: A competing submission by Burnley and Pendle councils (28 Nov 2025); not selected. Groupings triangulated from the Lancaster City Council LGR report (para 15e) plus Burnley/Pendle coverage; all districts kept whole. Populations other than the East unit (~270,000, first-party Pendle figure) and the South unit (358,947) are unverified.
